offence_severity: Life imprisonment u/s 302/149 and 7 years rigorous imprisonment u/s 307/149
physical_harm: Two persons died of fire-arm injuries and others suffered fire-arm injuries
number_of_offences: Charged with multiple offences, convictions upheld for causing death and injuries
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as motive was not disputed
motive: Bad blood between accused and complainant related to daughter and vehicle charges
key_evidence_accepted: There is ample evidence to support the prosecution case that accused came with firearms and opened fire on complainant party - It is an undisputed fact that two persons died of fire-arm injuries and all the injuries suffered by others were also fire-arm injuries.
witness_credibility: The High Court has rightly held that having regard to the nature of evidence tendered by them, there were no good grounds to discard their version. The injuries sustained by the witnesses were duly supported by medical evidence - both documentary as well as oral - through PWs-5, 6, 7 and 8. There was nothing pointed out in the evidence of PWs-1 to 4 to discredit their version.
bail_history: Appellant Soma in Criminal Appeal No.1158/2008 who is on bail is directed to surrender before Magistrate forthwith for serving out the remaining period of sentence, if any
trial_duration: The trial court convicted the accused u/ss 147, 148, 302/149 and 307/149 and sentenced them to imprisonment for life u/s 302/149 and 7 years RI u/s 307/149. The High Court confirmed the conviction and the sentences.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court: Not specified in the text provided.
investigation_status: FIR was factually recorded without delay on the basis whereof the investigation started; and in the absence of any other infirmity in that respect, the delay in forwarding the report to the Magistrate does not in any way vitiate the case of the prosecution.
appeal_history: The appeals were dismissed by the Supreme Court. The High Court confirmed the conviction and sentences. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced them.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused opened fire on the complainant party, causing the death of two persons and injuries to others. The evidence supported the prosecution's case that the accused were armed with firearms and that the injuries were caused by gunshots. The FIR was recorded without delay, and the investigation started based on it.
defence_argument: The appellants contended that there was a delay in filing the FIR and in forwarding the express report to the Magistrate, which vitiated the prosecution case. They also argued that the principle of common object could not be applied to the nature of the offences punishable under Sections 302, 307, and 149, and that the expression 'other offence' in Section 141 'Third' should be restricted to similar offences of mischief or criminal trespass.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the expression 'other offence' in Section 141 'Third' should be interpreted broadly to include any offence punishable under the IPC, and that the principle of 'ejusdem generis' cannot be applied to restrict it to only mischief or criminal trespass.
precedent_relied_upon: Sandeep v. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2012 (5) SCR 952; Bhajan Singh @ Harbhajansingh and Ors. v. State of Haryana, 2011 (7) SCR 1; Shiv Lal & Another v. State of Chhattisgarh, 2011 (11) SCR 429; State of Maharashtra v. Chandraprakash Kewalchand Jain, 1990 (1) SCR 115; State of U.P. v. Pappu, 2004 (6) Suppl. SCR 585; State of Punjab v. Gunnit Singh, 1996 (1) SCR 532; State of Orissa v. Thakara Besra, 2002 (3) SCR 173; State of H.P. v. Raghubir Singh, 1993 (2) SCR 17; Wahid Khan v. State of M.P., 2009 (15) SCR 1207; Rameshwar v. State of Rajasthan, 1952 SCR 377
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the accused committed a grave offence of causing death and injuries through the use of firearms, and the courts below correctly convicted and sentenced them under Sections 302, 307, 147, and 148 of the IPC.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The court weighed the aggravating factors such as the use of firearms, the resulting deaths and serious injuries, and the lack of any justification for the violence.
